faq.q: What specific material properties make Titanium Multi-Port Gas Manifold suitable for Monoblock multi-port gas mixing manifold?
faq.a: Titanium Multi-Port Gas Manifold uses Grade 2 CP-Ti because its yield strength, fatigue endurance, and corrosion resistance directly address gas delivery operational demands. The alloy's specific strength enables mass reduction without section compromise, while the TiO2 passivation ensures long-term environmental resistance.

faq.q: What are the critical dimensional tolerances for Titanium Multi-Port Gas Manifold?
faq.a: Standard machining tolerance for Titanium Multi-Port Gas Manifold is +/-0.05mm (ISO 2768-m). Functional mating surfaces are held to +/-0.025mm with Ra 0.8um finish, verified specifically for monoblock multiport gas requirements. Threaded features conform to ISO 965-2 Class 6g, verified with calibrated Go/No-Go ring gauges on 100% of production.

faq.q: Does Titanium Multi-Port Gas Manifold require any post-machining surface treatment?
faq.a: Yes. monoblock multiport gas components require Electropolishing Ra <0.25um + UHP DI cascade rinse with particle count verification per MIL-STD-1246 Class 1 — tailored for monoblock multiport gas application. This restores the natural TiO2 passive layer removed during machining and provides the required surface properties for the specific service environment. Key parameters include surface finish Ra 0.8um and passive layer thickness verification per applicable standards.

faq.q: What quality documentation is included with Titanium Multi-Port Gas Manifold shipments?
faq.a: Each shipment of Titanium Multi-Port Gas Manifold includes: (1) EN 10204 Type 3.1 MTR with full chemical analysis and mechanical properties; (2) Certificate of Conformance confirming all processes meet monoblock multiport gas specifications; (3) Dimensional inspection report with actual vs nominal measurements on critical features; (4) Surface roughness certification per applicable standards. FAIR available on request.
